title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Context from the previous page. Grothendieck considers a rational Hodge structure (V_Q, V_C = ⊕V^{pq}) with Mumford–Tate group G. He adds a k-structure V_k ⊂ V_C, for a subfield k ⊂ C, compatible with the Hodge filtration. He asks when such a triple (V_Q, Hodge decomposition, V_k) comes from a motive over k. The intended dictionary is V_Q = Betti realization, V_k = de Rham realization over k, and the inclusion V_k ⊂ V_C is the comparison isomorphism.

Necessary conditions (previous page). Assuming the Hodge conjecture, the motivic Galois group G' of the motive, defined over k via the fibre functor T_DR, satisfies G'_C = G°_C. So G°_C must be definable over k through V_k. Equivalently, after a finite extension k'/k, every Hodge tensor in the tensor algebra of V ⊕ V' must lie in the k'-structure: it must be k'-rational for the de Rham structure.

The counterexample (previous page). Take k = Q and V_k = V_Q. The Hodge filtration is then defined over Q, which forces the Hodge structure to be of Tate type (p,p). The Mumford–Tate group is then a torus defined over Q, so the conditions above hold. But no motive realizes it: for Q(1) the comparison involves 2πi, which is not rational.

This page. Grothendieck concludes: 'Il faut donc compléter les conditions néc. précédentes par des conditions du type "conj. de transcendance", pour éliminer le contre-exemple précédent.' He first wrote 'conjectures', struck it out, and replaced it with 'conditions'. So any characterization of motivic triples must include transcendence conditions on the comparison isomorphism (the periods), not only algebraic or Tannakian ones.

Next page. He sets up G = Aut_K(T), the torsor P = Isom_K(T_K, T'), and a point g ∈ P(L), with g taken modulo G(K). This is the period torsor, with the comparison isomorphism as an L-point of it. The natural transcendence condition is that g be a generic point of P, or of a suitable K-subvariety. This is the Grothendieck period conjecture in its torsor form.
errors: No error. The statement is programmatic. Implicitly, transcendence-type conditions are still not shown to be sufficient; whether the algebraic conditions plus a genericity condition on periods would characterize motivic triples is left open.

ideas.what: Hodge structures with a k-structure compatible with the Hodge filtration as candidate realizations of motives over k; necessary condition: the Mumford–Tate group is definable over k via the de Rham structure (Hodge tensors are de Rham-rational)
ideas.modern_name: Absolute Hodge / de Rham-rationality of Hodge classes; motivic Galois group versus Mumford–Tate group; realization categories (Deligne, Jannsen)
ideas.where_published: Ideas present in Grothendieck's 1960s motive correspondence; not in EGA/SGA

ideas.what: Algebraic or Tannakian conditions are insufficient; transcendence conditions on periods are required (the counterexample k = Q, V_k = V_Q ruled out by irrationality/transcendence of 2πi)
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck period conjecture (transcendence degree of periods equals dimension of the motivic Galois group; the period point is generic in the period torsor)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (1966 footnote), formulated in torsor form by André; also Lang and Ayoub, Kontsevich–Zagier
ideas.where_published: Footnote in 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties' (Publ. IHES 29, 1966); discussed in André's books

missed.claim: Grothendieck poses the problem of characterizing which Hodge structures with a compatible k-structure come from motives over k. He proposes necessary conditions of two kinds: Mumford–Tate group definable over k, and transcendence/genericity of periods. No conjectural 'if and only if' characterization of this kind (a Hodge–de Rham analogue of Fontaine–Mazur) is standard in the literature.
missed.quote: Il faut donc compléter les conditions néc. précédentes par des conditions du type "conj. de transcendance", pour éliminer le contre-exemple précédent.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A conjectural characterization of the essential image of the Betti–de Rham realization in terms of Mumford–Tate data plus period genericity is still lacking. The page shows Grothendieck framing the period conjecture as part of exactly this recognition problem, not merely as a statement about transcendence degree.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an early (1965) manuscript appearance of the idea behind the Grothendieck period conjecture, motivated by an explicit counterexample and framed as part of a 'which Hodge+de Rham data are motivic' problem. The period conjecture itself is known and credited to him; the recognition-problem framing is a modestly interesting unpublished detail.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'Il faut donc compléter les conditions néc. précédentes' is consistent with the image; 'donc' is plausible.
Line 2: 'conjectures' struck out, replaced above the line by 'conditions'; then 'du type "conj. de transcendance",'.
Line 3: 'pour éliminer le contre-exemple précédent.' Confirmed.
